newsitem.title: USA: US high-sulphur resid pressured by growing supply.
newsitem.headline: US high-sulphur resid pressured by growing supply.

text.p: U.S. spot high-sulphur residual fuel oil prices were pressured by growing supply in Gulf Coast and softer crude values Monday.
"We got a lot out here," said a Houston trader, referring to the rising number of high-sulphur barrels in the Gulf.

He attributed coker problems at several Gulf refineries to more high-sulfur materials offers in the market in recent weeks. A coker unit processes heavy streams such as resids into light-end products such as distillates and gasoline.
Although producers have attempted to export the barrels, current demand has been unable to absorb the excess supply.
Softer bunker fuel prices in Europe were contributed to today's bearish tone in high-sulphur trading, traders said.
The New York Power Authority (NYPA) bought 100,000 barrels of 0.3 percent sulphur high-pour No 6 fuel grade in a range of $22.50-$23.00/bbl at a tender today, market sources said.

With pressure on low- and high-sulphur materials, New York Harbor one pct was assessed 25 cents/bbl lower in a range of $21.50-$21.75. January one pct paper dipped to $21.25-$21.75 from Friday's $21.75-$22.00.

High sulphurs in New York market slipped as 2.2 percent dropped to $17.75 from $18.13 Friday. NYH 0.3 percent high pour grade was pegged in line with NYPA's purchase at $22.50-$23.00 against Friday's $23.00.

U.S. Gulf Coast one percent grade stayed near $18.63, while three percent was steady at $15.50-$16.00 amid the lack of actual trades. January three pct paper was quoted in a $16.50-$16.60 range, narrower than Friday's $16.50-$16.85.
New York city gate gas prices fell to $4.28-$4.30/mmBtu, sharply lower than Friday's $4.90-$5.00 but higher than NYH one percent resid at a $3.43/mmBtu equivalent.
